aciklama: Special steel alloy casting. Draws very high current from the grid; must be scheduled for the night to avoid peak demand charges.
Barrel tempering. Once heated, it cannot be stopped for 8 hours (uninterruptible constraint).
Barrel rifling. Short duration but draws extremely high instantaneous (peak) power.
Armor plate cutting. Can be flexibly shifted to daytime solar (PV) hours or nighttime depending on need.
Weapon body machining. Draws low-to-medium power. Can easily fill daytime production gaps.
Transforms sheet metal into car chassis. Must be optimized to avoid pushing daytime grid peak (demand) limits.
Body paint baking process. Draws continuous thermal power from the grid and the process cannot be interrupted.
Performance testing of finished engines. Draws high power but can return energy to the grid during braking phases.
Bumper and console production. Consumes fluctuating power during mold closing and melt injection phases.
Total load of 6-axis robotic arms during welding. Optimized according to the speed of the production line.
The 15 MW machine that will blow the jury's mind. Shakes the transformer of the entire industrial zone. Must be locked to 03:00 AM.
Gigantic drive motors that crush steel billets into plates. Draws very heavy power.
Maintains the temperature of liquid steel before casting. Consumes continuously high energy during the holding phase.
Critical line that pours liquid steel into molds to form billets, absolutely intolerant to interruptions.
Produces the massive pneumatic pressure for the facility. Only runs during cheap hours to store air in tanks.
